I've been growing cotton on this land for most of my life. My mother grew it before me on nearby fields. Quzhou is cotton country — the soil knows it, and so do I.

With 13.1 mu all in cotton, I won't change what works. Some younger farmers in the village have been experimenting with other crops, but cotton is what I know, what the local gin accepts, and what gives me predictable income even when prices dip. My husband helps during peak season but works construction in Handan most months, so I need a crop I can manage mostly alone.

**Variety**: I'll buy Bt hybrid cotton seeds again this year — probably from the same seed dealer in town I've used for the past decade. Ever since Bt cotton came in, I spend so much less time spraying for bollworm. My arms used to ache from the pump sprayer in summer. Worth every extra fen per seed.

**Tillage**: Rotary tillage. I hire the tractor neighbor for one pass before planting. Deep ploughing every few years is enough — I did it two seasons ago.

**Fertilizer**: I apply compound fertilizer as base before covering the seeds, then top-dress with urea during the boll-setting stage when plants are flowering heavily. This is what my father taught me and what the extension station confirmed years ago. I don't use too much — I've seen neighbors burn their plants.

**Irrigation**: I'll irrigate about 4 times from the well. Once before planting to wet the seedbed. Again if May is dry during seedling establishment. The critical one is during boll formation in July. Then once more in August if it's a dry year, which it usually is lately.

**Pesticides**: Even with Bt seeds, I spray for aphids in June — they come every year without fail — and for spider mites and whiteflies later. About 5 or 6 times total. I'm careful about alternating chemicals because I've seen resistance build up.

**Yield expectation**: A good year gives me 300 kg/mu of seed cotton. Last year was a bit dry and I got 270. I'll plan for 280 as a realistic middle estimate.
